answer: Each identity appraises one basalt lot in the grove: it locks a 70-credit bond and posts a sealed appraisal. A grove auditor recomputes the value from public past sales of basalt and comparable cedar lots. A mismatch beyond 5 percent or a reused appraisal burns the bond. The first booking costs 30 credits; the kth identity from one source pays 30+4(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 4,026 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,028,000 plus 70,000 bonded. A rented-appraisal ring fails because each appraisal binds one key to one basalt hash and one comparable set. An honest appraiser pays 30 once and recovers the bond.
